enforcing_note: Enforcing since 2026-09-30: every counted unit is above the floor, so a unit below it, a total below it or a first-party file no test loads fails coverage_floor (full tier) and scripts/coverage.sh. Units are derived from the path, so a new crate, plugin or editor is judged from its first file. An exemption is for what cannot be instrumented at all, never for what is merely untested -- exempt for a unit, exempt_files for one file inside a counted unit -- and each is audited for a reason and a file that still exists.

exempt.modules/trance-gate: ui_chain.js, 1315 lines that run on the Move inside Schwung's shadow UI: it imports Schwung's own page controller, input filter and screen reader by their absolute paths on the device (/data/UserData/schwung/shared/...), which this repository does not carry, so nothing here can load it. engines/trance-gate/tests/smoke_ui.mjs runs every entry point against those shared sources in the module's own build (engines/trance-gate/tests/run.sh), outside this report. The module's DSP is tg-core and its C shell is tg-move, both counted. A real gap, stated rather than hidden.

exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ui/gallery/Main.cpp: The gallery application's entry point: a JUCEApplication that opens a desktop window and runs the event loop until a person closes it, so no test binary links it (tests/ui links the gallery's pages, not the app). Everything it shows is counted: every page, through the kit's tests and their snapshots (tests/ui), and the frame and registry in Gallery.cpp (tests/ui/gallery.cpp). The --shots mode it adds writes pictures for a person to look at, which the snapshot tests already hold.
exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ni/FileDialog.mm: AppKit's NSSavePanel and NSOpenPanel shown as sheets on an editor's window: compiled only into the plugin-format targets (cmake/NiPlugin.cmake), and a panel needs a window server and a person to answer it, so no test binary can drive it. Everything around it is counted: the text it moves is tg-core's slotfile.rs and the shell's tg_shell_export / tg_shell_import (tg-core, tg-capi), and the file I/O and the words the editor shows are Patch.cpp's ExportFile / ImportFile (tg_state). The editor's side of the message path runs in the e2e suite against the mock host.
exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ni/Clipboard.mm: AppKit's NSPasteboard, the user's general clipboard: compiled only into the plugin-format targets (cmake/NiPlugin.cmake), and a test that wrote to it would overwrite whatever the person running the tests had copied. It is behind the ni::Clipboard interface so everything around it is counted with a fake standing in: what Copy and Paste put on and take off the clipboard and the words the editor shows are Patch.cpp's CopySlot / Paste (tg_state), the text is tg-core's slotfile.rs and paste.rs and the shell's tg_shell_export / tg_shell_paste (tg-core, tg-capi), and the editor's side runs in the e2e suite against the mock host's clipboard.
exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ni/WebPlugin.cpp: ni::WebPlugin derives from iplug::Plugin, and IPlug_include_in_plug_hdr.h stops with #error outside a plugin-format target while iplug_configure_target refuses any other kind -- so no test binary can link it, and only a host loading a bundle runs it (tg_au, sc_au, the validators), never an instrumented object. What it decides rather than forwards is counted where it was lifted to: the editor protocol in Editor.cpp (ni_editor, over a recording Port) and every quantiser, height and transport rule in Wire.cpp (ni_wire).
exempt_files.plugins/trance-gate/TranceGate.cpp: The plugin class, which compiles only inside a plugin-format target (see WebPlugin.cpp's entry). Params.cpp and Patch.cpp, lifted out of it to be tested, are counted. What is left is calls into iPlug2 and the engine, plus two small pieces of logic not yet lifted -- WidthMs's walk to field 12 of the params readout, and SendGate's unchanged-patch cache -- which only tg_au and the validators reach, against a bundle.
exempt_files.plugins/side-chain/SideChain.cpp: The plugin class, which compiles only inside a plugin-format target (see WebPlugin.cpp's entry). Params.cpp and Wire.cpp (the input routing and the duplicate-key test), lifted out of it to be tested, are counted. What is left is fifteen parameter stores, the MIDI forward and the block loop around sc_core_process_f32_split_tap, which sc_au renders through a real AU host against the engine's own output, sample for sample -- against a bundle, so outside this report.
exempt_files.plugins/spectrogram/Spectrogram.cpp: The plugin class, which compiles only inside a plugin-format target (see WebPlugin.cpp's entry). State.cpp and Wire.cpp, lifted out of it to be tested, are counted, and so are the analyzer and the receiver it drives (spectro-core, spectro-recv, spectro-capi). What is left and still logic is ServiceReceiver's rebuild of the receiver on a rate change and the editor-message dispatch; neither is reached by any test here, which is a gap this entry states rather than covers.
exempt_files.plugins/listen-in/ListenIn.cpp: The plugin class, which compiles only inside a plugin-format target (see WebPlugin.cpp's entry). State.cpp and Wire.cpp, lifted out of it to be tested, are counted, and so is the transport (bus-core, bus-capi; abus_ipc across processes and architectures). ServiceBus -- release first, then claim, and wait while the audio thread still holds the old pusher -- is the largest piece of logic still inside a plugin class and no test here reaches it: the next candidate to lift out, as State.cpp was.
